page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-16GB is a cloud server configuration featuring the AMD EPYC 9575F processor running on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization. The instance provisions 2 shared virtual CPU cores clocked at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a substantial 8.0 GB per core. The server includes 150 GB of bundled local SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. Discrete graphics accelerators are absent, with a GPU count of zero. The CPU provides comprehensive instruction set support, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES cryptography, and BMI2 instructions.

Benchmark testing demonstrates high single-threaded performance contrasted with limited parallel throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core testing (3756.97) and Geekbench single-core evaluations (2248.0), complemented by leading single-thread data processing metrics in gzip compression (38.22 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.95 GB/sec). However, multi-core capacity is bounded by the two-vCPU allocation, yielding weak rankings in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core workloads, and software compilation tasks. Memory throughput reaches 68.14 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 50.81 GB/sec for writes, while static web serving throughput measures 7.52 GB/sec.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the combination of shared CPU allocation with a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. While the instance provides high single-thread efficiency and considerable memory headroom per thread, the low core count and shared execution model make it ill-suited for dense parallel tasks, large-scale Redis deployments, or multi-threaded machine learning inference on models of 7B parameters or larger. Cost efficiency is driven primarily by resource density, pairing substantial memory and local storage on a minimal compute footprint. Workload compatibility centers on single-threaded utilities, lightweight databases, in-memory caching nodes, text processing pipelines, and low-concurrency web hosting.
description: The UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-16GB is an x86_64 virtual instance powered by a 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC 9575F processor running under KVM. Configured with 2 shared vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, it establishes a high 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 150 GB of bundled local SSD storage and no discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core compute and fast single-threaded compression speeds, though total multi-threaded performance is naturally constrained by the dual-vCPU count. Memory bandwidth remains solid across both cached and uncached block tests, and static web serving delivers stable throughput. With its high memory allocation relative to compute cores, this configuration provides practical cost efficiency for memory-dependent tasks that rely on strong single-threaded CPU responsiveness, including modest relational databases, memory caching layers, text processing, and web serving.
